Sure, here are two hints for the given step:

Hint 1: Consider the definition of Mean Squared Error (MSE) for a constant model. The MSE is calculated as the average of the squared differences between the actual target values $y_i$ and the predicted values $\hat{y}_i$. For a constant model, $\hat{y}_i $$=$$ 	heta_0$ for all $i$. Think about how you can adjust $	heta_0$ to minimize these squared differences.

Hint 2: Recall that the derivative of a function gives us the slope of the function at any point. To find the minimum of the MSE with respect to $	heta_0$, you need to take the derivative of the MSE with respect to $	heta_0$ and set it to zero. This will help you find the value of $	heta_0$ that minimizes the MSE. Consider what statistical measure of the target values $y_i$ might correspond to this optimal $	heta_0$.
